correctness.rationale: Exact 4D lattice coordinates and Striker Theorem 3.3 establish the full eight-facet presentation. All 256 subsets of these facets are exhaustively intersected with the seven vertices and ranked exactly: 7 vertices, 17 edges, 18 two-faces, eight facets. The gcd-of-minors saturated lattice test shows exactly five nonsmooth normal cones of dimension three, with every other nonsmooth cone contained in them. Each four-ray relation is a primitive unit-square relation and all triples are saturated, giving the transverse affine toric node ab-cd. The standard toric orbit-cone and Q-factoriality criteria justify the global statement. An extracted standalone integer/rational checker reproduces these finite certificates; no infinite extrapolation is used.

evidence: The size-three Birkhoff polytope has six vertices and nine facets, while ASM3 has seven vertices and eight, so their normal fans differ. The known ASM vertex/facet theorem proves the input but is not a classification of saturated normal cones. The all-size even-cycle stable-set toric classifications located in the accessible research history explicitly start beyond the four-cycle and therefore do not imply this boundary case.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Geometric implications were compared, not just titles: Birkhoff is a proper subpolytope and its nine-curve toric singular configuration does not descend to ASM3; the four-cycle stable-set formulation is exactly equivalent and must be checked as such. No searched stronger coverage was established. Remaining uncertainty is not presented as proof of uniqueness.

The present finding identifies the complete normal-fan toric singular support and integral equivalence with the C4 stable-set polytope. Searches of those relevant full texts and the queried mathematical records found no statement or stronger theorem implying this complete classification. Equivalent C4 graph-polytope coverage remains an explicit risk.

value.rationale: The first non-Birkhoff ASM polytope is a natural minimal test case of matrix-enumeration toric geometry. An explicit integral connection to the four-cycle stable-set polytope is a structural bridge between distinct combinatorial families, and the exact five-component node-curve support and incidence supply a complete natural geometric invariant absent from the inspected facet and Ehrhart descriptions. The computation identifies where the normal toric fourfold is non-Q-factorial and supplies a concrete basis for later higher-size study, without claiming a larger theorem.
